Guides

Creating an online shop: where to start?

Selling online is not just putting products on the internet. You need to think about payment, shipping and a few rules. Nothing impossible, as long as you take things in order.

An online shop: what is it exactly?

It is a website where your customers choose products, put them in a basket and pay by card. You receive the order, prepare the parcel and send it. Your shop stays open at night, on Sundays and while you are on holiday.

Step 1: choose where to start

The classic mistake is wanting to put everything online at once. Start with your best products, the ones people ask for most. The package includes up to 20 products that I add for you. That is plenty to get started and see what sells.

Step 2: photos and descriptions that sell

Online, customers cannot touch or try anything. Your photos and your words do the salesperson's job.

  • Photos: a plain background, daylight, several angles, and one photo that shows the real size of the item.
  • Description: material, size, care, and above all what the product is for and who it is for.

You send me the photos and a few notes. Lia writes the product pages, I check them, you approve.

Step 3: payment

Secure card payment is included in the shop. The money goes to your bank account, and the customer gets a confirmation email. You never see card numbers: everything goes through a specialist payment service.

Step 4: delivery

This is the point people forget most often, yet it decides your margin. Before opening, answer these questions:

  • Which countries do you deliver to?
  • Which carrier, and at what price depending on weight?
  • Do you offer free delivery above a certain amount?
  • Do you offer local pickup?

Weigh your products once packed before setting shipping costs: the box and the padding count in the weight.

Step 5: the rules to follow

Selling online to consumers comes with a few obligations: showing terms and conditions of sale, displaying prices including all taxes, and respecting the 14-day right of withdrawal for most products. A basic set of terms of sale comes with the shop. You complete it with your own delivery and returns rules.

How much does it cost

  • Building the shop: €500, with €125 when you order and €375 when it goes live.
  • A monthly plan from €5 for hosting, the domain name and updates.
  • Two options just for shops, at €5 a month each: stock tracking, and customer accounts so your buyers can find their orders.

The payment service takes a small fee on each sale. This is the case for every online shop, whatever solution you choose.

Step 6: bring in visitors

A shop with no visitors sells nothing. Tell your current customers, slip the address into every parcel and onto your packaging, and think about SEO: every well-written product page is a way in from Google.

Your questions

How many products can I sell?

The package includes putting 20 products online. You can then add more using the changes in your plan. For a much larger catalogue from the start, the shop is built on a quote.

Do I need a registered business to sell online?

Yes. Selling regularly, even in small amounts, means having a declared business, for example as a micro-entrepreneur. Look into it before you open: it is quick and done online.

Can I keep my physical shop and add an online shop?

Yes, it is actually a great fit. The stock tracking option stops you selling online an item that has just sold in store.
